text:
Lars Eller played his 1,200th NHL game on Nov. 4 against Chicago, and RMNB carried his line about the journey from Denmark: "The little kid would be proud today." He's 37, on his seventh NHL team, and he's playing more than he has in years: up almost three minutes a game over his last ten.

His 8 points in 18 games are a nice surprise. He has one goal on 2.91 expected, so the finishing is behind, but Florida has scored about 4.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has helped the assists. The Panthers out-shoot teams with him (57% of attempts) but take only 49% of the expected goals, and they're better without him.

That fits Evolving-Hockey's read from last season: offense isn't his game, with his team creating fewer chances with him on the ice than with almost any other forward (bottom 2%). His value has to come from elsewhere: matchups, experience, and filling holes while Florida deals with injuries. He has a 2018 Cup from Washington. We project about 36 points. The more interesting number is the minutes: when a 37-year-old's ice time rises in November, it tells you how thin the lineup has become.
headline: Lars Eller, 1,200 games in
